solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Husband replaces wife in guardian's set

indicators.note: to replace is to take another's place, so one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: a warden is a guardian or keeper
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A domestic shuffle: the husband takes the wife's place in some guardian's household arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: The W at the front of WARDEN becomes H. 'Set' looks like a noun (a group or collection) but is the verb, as concrete or jelly sets.
explanation.definitionFit: When glue, cement or jelly sets it becomes firm and solid, which is exactly what hardening means.

clue.text: Animal starts to hatch young ever nearer April

indicators.note: the start of each word is its opening letter, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Some animal is getting ready to hatch its young as April approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The springtime story of hatching is a cover; only the initial letters of the last five words matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is an African carnivorous mammal, a specific example of the broad category named.

clue.text: Make a further request for a non- Tory judge

indicators.note: 'non' says the thing named must be absent, so that letter is struck out

parts.note: a recorder is a part-time judge in English courts
C is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories

explanation.surface: Someone asks again, this time for a judge who isn't a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: A recorder is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a part-time judge in England; take the C out of RECORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To order something again is to place a second or repeat request for goods, the commercial sense of the word.

clue.text: Awful former king having the means to besiege the city

indicators.note: an army besieging a place surrounds it on all sides, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: EX means former and R (rex) is king
EC is the postcode for the City of London
able means having the means or capacity to do something

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch with the resources to lay siege to the capital was a dreadful ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former king' is split around the city rather than kept together. In crosswords 'the city' is the City of London, the financial district, identified by its postcode letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable describes something extremely bad or detestable, a stronger synonym for dreadful or terrible.

clue.text: I'm backing superior song by Edith Piaf

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a lord is a superior, one who rules over others

explanation.surface: Someone claims to support a fine song by the French singer Edith Piaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like musical accompaniment, fitting a song, but it turns the short word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Milord is a 1959 hit recording by the French chanteuse Edith Piaf, so the answer is a specific example of her songs.

clue.text: On good terms with nudists regularly found in Greenland

definitions.note: the answer is a people, not a phrase; read as 'people found in Greenland'

parts.note: to be in with someone is to be on good terms with them

indicators.note: doing something at regular intervals means taking every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone is friendly with naturists who turn up in Greenland, an unlikely place to be unclothed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: it describes the answer as those found in Greenland rather than naming them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are the indigenous Arctic people who make up most of Greenland's population.

clue.text: Not a cog in circulation with eight angles

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun answer: a figure with eight angles

indicators.note: something in circulation is moving round and about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A coin or part with eight corners is said not to be a gear cog in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In circulation' suggests coins, apt since some coins are eight-sided, but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a polygon defined by having eight sides and eight interior angles.

clue.text: Corruption is centre of concern after ten years

indicators.note: coming after means placed later in the line, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years

indicators.note: the centre is the middle part, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the middle three of its seven letters

explanation.surface: After a decade of power, corruption becomes the central worry.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of a seven-letter word here is three letters, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral decline and self-indulgence, close in sense to corruption or degeneracy.

clue.text: Reproduced mid-term vote to accept Obama initially covered by Times journalist

indicators.note: taking something on means adding it, so these parts are joined in a row
being covered by something means having it added, here as the following part

parts.note: a voter marks the ballot with a cross

indicators.note: the middle of a word is what lies between its ends, so only the central letters stay

parts.note: the two central letters

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
the multiplication sign
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Coverage of the US mid-term elections, with Obama's name reported by a newspaper journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is not the newspaper but the multiplication sign. The joining words are loose; the pieces simply run X, ER, O, X, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerox is a brand of photocopier, so to xerox a page is to photocopy or reproduce it.

clue.text: Only something cold will produce the right outcome

parts.note: just means only, as in 'just one'
ice is something cold

explanation.surface: A claim that only a cold-blooded approach brings about a fair result.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the saying that revenge is a dish best served cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice is fairness achieved, the morally proper result when wrongs are dealt with.

clue.text: A swift polish won't hold you up

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun: something that will not support you

parts.note: quick means swift
to sand a surface is to smooth or polish it

explanation.surface: A quick buff of your shoes won't delay you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold you up' reads as delay, but the sense is physical support: you sink rather than stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicksand is loose waterlogged sand that cannot bear weight, so anyone standing on it sinks.

clue.text: Urge to go somewhere else wasn't ruled out of order

indicators.note: things out of order are not in their proper sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A wish to move elsewhere was not dismissed, the chair said, as out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruled out of order' sounds like a chairman's procedural ruling, but 'out of order' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderlust is a strong desire to travel and roam, borrowed from German.

clue.text: Saunters gaily about deck, smoking primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone strolls happily round a ship's deck with a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a full description of a stroll, but after the definition only the initials count.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about is to wander idly in search of pleasure, much like sauntering around.

clue.text: Republican Bush mistaken for another one

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrong or garbled, so the letters come out in another order

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Republican named Bush is confused with another of the same name, as the two presidents often were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another one' refers back to 'bush' read as a plant: the answer is another word for a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, a near synonym for a bush.

clue.text: Wisely secretive about worker eating a pasty

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: sly means furtive or secretive

indicators.note: something eating takes another inside it

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple
a pasty is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: A worker tucks into a pasty, being cagey about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the worker eats the pie first, then the secretive word wraps the result. A pasty is a Cornish pastry turnover filled with meat and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient means wise or discerning, so acting sapiently is acting with wisdom.

clue.text: Surgeon admits grandma following a firm promise

indicators.note: following means coming after, so one part is placed after the other

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
nan is a British word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A surgeon takes in an elderly relative after a company makes a firm pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm promise' looks like one phrase, but 'firm' belongs with 'a' and 'promise' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding agreement or solemn pledge, a weightier word for promise.

clue.text: Successfully defend retired detectives framed by absurdly naive terrorist leader

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run the other way
a picture framed by something sits within it, so one piece goes inside
something absurd is nonsensical, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A legal win: clearing police officers caught up with a gullible terror suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Framed' suggests the detectives were set up, a fitting criminal note, but it signals placing inside. CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of UK police.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate someone is to clear them of blame or prove a disputed position right, which is defending it successfully.

clue.text: Dad returned tool used for spreading on glue etc

definitions.text: used for spreading on glue etc
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a plural noun: things used for spreading

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
pliers are a gripping hand tool

explanation.surface: Father brings back a tool he borrowed for gluing jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tool used for spreading' looks like one phrase defining a tool, but 'tool' is wordplay and the definition starts at 'used'.
explanation.definitionFit: Appliers are devices or people that apply a substance, such as spreading adhesive onto a surface.

clue.text: Money is invested in South Asian country for Peruvians say in America

indicators.note: capital invested in a venture is put into it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Laos is a country in South-East Asia
tin is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Funds poured into an Asian nation, apparently for the benefit of Peruvians living in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is old British slang for cash. 'Say' marks Peruvians as one example of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Latinos are people of Latin American origin living in the United States, so Peruvian Americans are one example.

clue.text: Possibly count on coming back with half a rouble

indicators.note: coming back means heading the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: half of a word is a part of it, here its last three letters

parts.note: the back three of its six letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps you can count on getting back half your Russian money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb, but it is the title of a European nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a European aristocrat, so a count is one example of a nobleman; 'possibly' marks the example.

clue.text: Restriction on district relief is an anti-poverty initiative

parts.note: a ban is a restriction
D is a standard abbreviation for district
aid is relief given to people in need

explanation.surface: Capping local relief payments is presented as a measure to fight poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like policy jargon; each word supplies a piece in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Band Aid was the 1984 charity supergroup organised by Bob Geldof to raise money for famine relief in Ethiopia.

clue.text: Relish spirit of the age at both extremes

indicators.note: only the extreme ends survive, so everything between them is dropped

parts.note: zeitgeist is German for the spirit of the age

explanation.surface: Someone savours the mood of the times in all its extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: Two letters from each end of ZEITGEIST are kept: the extremes here are pairs, not single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is gusto or keen enjoyment, the same as relish in the sense of appetite for something.

clue.text: Get rid of form of nose pin no longer available

indicators.note: a new form of something reshapes it, so the letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
a dish that is off the menu is no longer available

explanation.surface: Discarding a type of nose stud that can no longer be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' is the restaurant sense: an item that has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pension someone off is to retire them, usually to be rid of them, hence dismiss or discard.

clue.text: Publicity over fish gives a sense of satisfaction

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so this part comes first

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Media attention about catching a fish leaves an angler feeling pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: The ide, a European carp-like fish, turns up in crosswords far more often than in rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride is the pleasure felt at one's own or another's achievement, a feeling of satisfaction.

clue.text: Safe-cracker is sadly not scarce counterfeiter

indicators.note: things gone sadly wrong are in a mess, so the leftover letters are rearranged
'not' says these letters are absent, so they are taken away

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen
these six letters are removed

explanation.surface: Safe-crackers are, unfortunately, plentiful, as are forgers.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, C, A, R, C, E from SAFECRACKER and the five letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A faker produces fraudulent imitations, which is what a counterfeiter does with money or goods.

clue.text: Useful tool I lent us is broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, which can be put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A handy gadget I loaned to us has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first two words; the rest reads as a complaint about a borrowed tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a practical implement, especially for kitchen use, a near synonym for a handy tool.

clue.text: Entertainment said to carry satisfactory ending for the audience

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words count for how they are pronounced
an audience listens, so what matters is what they hear

parts.note: satisfactory is OK, and the pair, spoken, run together

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A show reputedly brought to a happy conclusion for those watching.
explanation.walkthrough: The British pronunciation 'karry-oh-kee' makes the first part match 'carry OK'.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke is a form of amusement in which people sing along to recorded backing tracks, usually in bars.

clue.text: They follow orders for the Sabbath in an Arab country

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Yemen is a country on the Arabian Peninsula
S is short for Sabbath

explanation.surface: Observing a day of rest in Yemen means obeying the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: S for Sabbath is a less common abbreviation, but it appears in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are sycophants who agree with and obey superiors without question.

clue.text: Kind offer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to present formally, or a formal bid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind offer' reads as one phrase, a generous proposal, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for gentle affection and also a verb or noun for a formal bid, as in tendering for a contract.
